name: Hero Object
description: One 3D object lit in a dark studio (glossy or translucent material, soft key light, cool rim, floor shadow, bokeh), with a slow camera move and a lower-third title. Optional caption attached to the object with a fine leader line. The opening shot of a zoom: start from something the viewer can hold.

material.description: Material (default fits the object: ice-cube ice, glass-cube glass, drop water, coin metal, boot-sole rubber)

title.description: Lower-third title in bold caps, 2 to 7 words. Wrap the key word(s) in *asterisks*: they become the big line.

subtitle.description: Optional muted line under the title (10 words or fewer)

kicker.description: Optional tiny upper-case line above the title, e.g. "Part 1"

caption.description: Optional short label attached to the object with a leader line (2 to 5 words)

captionSub.description: Optional second line of the caption (a value or unit)

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleProps.title: Why is ice *slippery*?
exampleProps.subtitle: Start with something you can hold
exampleProps.caption: Frozen water

exampleNarration: Start with something ordinary, a cube of frozen water. Pick it up and it slides right out of your fingers. Why is ice so slippery?

name: Scale Dive
description: The signature shot: one continuous camera dive through 2 to 6 nested levels, outermost first (object, crystal lattice, molecule, atom, nucleus, quarks, or the liquid-like surface layer). Each level arrives on its spoken label with a lower-third (index, label, scale note); dust streams past during each dive. reverse: true plays the same list zooming OUT, for the "zoom back out" ending.

title.description: Optional headline shown before the first dive (7 words or fewer)

levels.description: 2 to 6 levels, outermost first. Each label should be spoken in the narration in visiting order (innermost first when reverse is true).

label.description: Short label, 1 to 3 words, spoken in the narration

note.description: Optional scale note, e.g. "centimetres" or "a tenth of a nanometre"

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

reverse.description: Zoom out through the same list (innermost to outermost)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

levels.label: Oxygen atom
levels.note: about a tenth of a nanometre

exampleNarration: Zoom into the ice cube. Inside is a crystal, a repeating stack of water molecules. Each water molecule holds one oxygen atom, and at its centre sits a tiny nucleus.

name: Crystal Lattice
description: Hexagonal ice in 3D: ball-and-stick water molecules (red oxygen, white hydrogen) linked by dashed hydrogen bonds, building in layer by layer on its keyword. Options: highlight the top or bottom layer, let the top layers turn disordered and liquid-like at a keyword, slide a skate blade, boot sole or ball across the surface, and up to 4 labels with leader lines.

title.description: Optional headline in bold caps (7 words or fewer); *words* in asterisks become the big line

keyword.description: Word the lattice finishes building on

highlight.description: Glow one layer and dim the rest

disorder.description: 0 to 1: how far the top layers break up into a liquid-like layer (0 = perfect crystal)

disorderKeyword.description: Word on which the top layers start to break up

disorderLayers.description: How many top bilayers break up, 1 or 2

slider.description: Optional object pressing or sliding on the surface

sliderKeyword.description: Word on which the slider arrives

hbonds.description: Show hydrogen bonds as dashed lines (default true)

labels.description: Up to 4 labels with leader lines

target.description: What the leader line points at

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: Inside, the molecules lock into a hexagonal lattice, held together by hydrogen bonds. But at the top, the molecules loosen into a thin, liquid-like layer, and the blade glides over it.

name: Molecule
description: One ball-and-stick molecule, large and slowly swaying in the studio. Presets (water with its 104.5 degree angle, carbon dioxide, methane, ammonia, oxygen, hydrogen) or your own atoms list. Options: partial-charge glow (coral = slightly negative, ice blue = slightly positive) with delta signs, a dipole arrow, the bond angle, and up to 4 labels.

preset.description: Molecule preset (ignored when atoms is given)

atoms.description: Optional custom molecule: up to 24 atoms. The first atom is the centre when no coordinates are given.

element.description: Element symbol: H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Na

bonds.description: Optional pairs of atom indices; default: bonds by distance

charges.description: Show partial charges (coral glow and delta minus on oxygen or nitrogen, ice glow and delta plus on hydrogen)

chargeKeyword.description: Word on which the charges appear

dipole.description: Show a dipole arrow beside the molecule

dipoleKeyword.description: Word on which the arrow grows

showAngle.description: Water only: draw the H-O-H angle with its value

angleKeyword.description: Word on which the angle draws

labels.description: Up to 4 labels with leader lines

target.description: oxygen, hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, bond, molecule, dipole, or an atom index as text

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: Here is one water molecule. An oxygen atom holds two hydrogens at a wide angle. The oxygen end is slightly negative, the hydrogen end slightly positive, so the whole molecule is a tiny dipole.

name: Particle Field
description: Many small glossy spheres (or tiny water molecules) behaving like matter at the molecular scale: roll (a loose layer rolling over a packed one, like ball bearings), jitter (thermal vibration that grows on the keyword), flow, settle (disordered to ordered) or scatter (ordered to disordered). Optional slab surface and up to 3 labels.

surface.description: Slab under the particles (default ice for roll, settle and scatter)

keyword.description: Word on which the behaviour starts or speeds up

labels.description: Up to 3 labels with leader lines

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: The loose molecules on top can roll over the solid ice below, a little like ball bearings under your feet.

name: Split Compare
description: Two studio vignettes side by side (stacked in tall), each a slowly turning 3D object with a title and up to 2 points, divided by a fine light line. For contrasts: solid versus liquid, before versus after, this material versus that one.

title.description: Optional headline over both sides (bold caps)

points.description: Up to 2 short points (6 words or fewer each)

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

points.description: Up to 2 short points (6 words or fewer each)

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: Compare the two. In ice, molecules are locked in an open lattice. In liquid water they tumble past each other, packed closer together, which is why ice floats.

name: Big Number
description: One large, heavy numeral counting to its value on the keyword (decimals, a true minus sign for negative values, a unit or word suffix), a label under it and a kicker above, over a slow, dimmed 3D object.

value.description: The number (negative values get a minus sign)

suffix.description: Optional unit or word, e.g. "°C", "%", " km", " billion"

label.description: What the number means (12 words or fewer)

kicker.description: Optional tiny upper-case line above the number

keyword.description: Word the count lands on

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleProps.label: Absolute zero, the coldest anything can be

exampleNarration: Nothing can get colder than minus two hundred seventy three point one five degrees Celsius, absolute zero.

name: Data Bars
description: 2 to 6 translucent ice bars in perspective, growing from a glass zero plane, each landing on its spoken label. Negative values hang downward from the zero line. Value labels at the bar ends, category labels at the zero line, optional highlighted bar and a small source note.

highlight.description: Label (or 0-based index) of the bar to highlight

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

note.description: Optional small source or condition note (bottom right)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: Melting points cover a wide range. Gallium melts at about thirty degrees, water at zero, seawater just below, and mercury near minus thirty nine.

name: Timeline
description: 2 to 6 dated events along a receding rail of light. A pulse travels the rail and each event node lights up as its date is spoken, with the date and a short label on a fine leader line.

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: In 1850 a liquid film on ice was first proposed. In 1886 came pressure melting. In 1939, friction heating. Today the surface layer is studied directly.

name: Title Card
description: Chapter card in bold documentary caps: a small kicker, a heavy title (the *emphasised* words become the big line) and a subtitle, over a slow, dimmed 3D backdrop (an object, the ice lattice or a water molecule). No accent lines.

title.description: 2 to 6 words; *words* in asterisks become the big, heaviest line

subtitle.description: Optional muted line (12 words or fewer)

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleProps.title: Into the *crystal*
exampleProps.subtitle: Where water stops flowing and starts stacking

exampleNarration: Chapter two. Into the crystal, where water stops flowing and starts stacking.

name: Quote Card
description: A short quote, cinematic and minimal: a heavy quote mark, bold caps revealed word by word with the voice, and the attribution, over drifting out-of-focus dust and a slow light sweep.

author.description: Who said or wrote it (no invented quotes from real people)

role.description: Optional muted line under the author

keyword.description: Word the quote starts on

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleProps.quote: Everything slippery has a *story* written in its surface.
exampleProps.author: A lab notebook

exampleNarration: Everything slippery has a story written in its surface.

name: Cause Chain
description: 2 to 5 steps, each a small turning 3D object with a label (and an optional note), linked by light paths that draw from one step to the next as each step is spoken. In a row in wide, a zigzag column in tall.

keyword.description: Optional word from the narration this element lands on (defaults to its label words)

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: The blade presses down, the surface molecules loosen, a thin water layer forms, and the skater glides.

name: Thumbnail
description: A single dramatic still for the video thumbnail (render one frame at 1280x720 from wide; tall also works). A big hero lit with a strong backlight and rim (an object, the ice lattice with an optional boot sole or skate blade pressing on it, or a molecule), 2 to 4 words of very large bold caps with a dark outline and backing, readable at 320 px wide, and an optional coral X strike or arrow on one word or on the hero. No accent bars.

slider.description: With hero crystal-lattice: an object pressing on the surface

preset.description: With hero molecule: the preset (default water)

text.description: 2 to 4 words; *words* in asterisks become the biggest line

side.description: Where the words go (wide): left (default) or right

word.description: 0-based index of the word to mark

sub.description: Optional second line, e.g. the authors

keyword.description: Word on which the box appears (default: 30 % into the scene)

exampleNarration: Why ice is slippery. It is not the pressure.
